Regulation · AI · Transparency

AI Act Article 50: what needs doing by 2 December 2026

Most of Article 50’s transparency duties have applied since 2 August 2026. For the machine-readable marking of generative AI already on the market, a transition period runs until 2 December 2026. A checklist for developers and operators.

Serge Zabolotny · 2026-10-27

  • EU AI Act
  • KI-Verordnung
  • Artikel 50
  • Transparenz
  • Kennzeichnung
  • Chatbot

What Article 50 requires

DutyWhoIn short
Chatbot disclosure (Art. 50(1))ProvidersPeople must be told they are interacting with AI – unless it is obvious
Machine-readable marking (para. 2)Providers of generative AISynthetic audio, image, video and text outputs must be marked as artificial, where technically feasible
Deep fakes (para. 4)DeployersDisclosure; do not rely on the provider’s marking
AI text on public-interest matters (para. 4)DeployersDisclosure, unless a person with editorial responsibility has reviewed the content

Disclosures must be clear, appear no later than the first interaction and be accessible. For breaches the source names a ceiling of up to €15 million or 3% of worldwide annual turnover.

The deadlines at a glance

  • 2 August 2026: most transparency duties apply.
  • 2 December 2026: transition period for machine-readable marking (para. 2) for generative AI systems already on the market before 2 August 2026 – introduced by the “Digital Omnibus” package. Background in The world in 10–20 years.
  • 20 July 2026: the Commission published the final guidelines on Article 50.
  • June 2026: the voluntary Code of Practice on transparency of AI-generated content was finalised; by the end of July about 190 organisations had signed, according to the source.

Checklist

  1. Do you have a chat or assistant? Then label it clearly as AI. The chat on this website carries the label “AI Assistant”; the guidelines read the “obvious” exception strictly, so an explicit label is the safe choice.
  2. Do you generate images, audio, video or text with AI for others? Check whether your provider supplies the machine-readable marking and plan for 2 December 2026.
  3. Do you publish AI text on matters of public interest? Either disclose it, or have a person with editorial responsibility review the substance. According to the source, the guidelines demand a genuine, knowledgeable review, not a cursory glance.
  4. Document the process: who reviews, by which criteria, and where is it recorded? My approach is in AI content with human-in-the-loop and the PflegeOasis case.
  5. Look at the Code of Practice: it is voluntary, but the Commission and the AI Board judged it adequate for paragraphs 2, 4 and 5.

Sources and limits

  • Reed Smith: Always read the label – EU AI transparency rules (law-firm article, as of October 2026)
  • Usercentrics: Digital Omnibus, high-risk deadlines and Article 50 (secondary source; please check the Official Journal yourself)

Not legal advice. I am a developer, not a lawyer. The details come from the sources listed (as of October 2026); the legal text is what counts.
